summary: 80-foot Aermotor LS-40 tower first built near Appleton, SC; sold by the state, moved about 3 miles, reconstructed on private land; current condition unconfirmed.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 steel tower, 80 ft, with 7 by 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: The 2013 register entry shows the tower reconstructed at its new site. A later Facebook post, whose visible text gives no date, calls pictures of it the ruins of the Appleton fire tower; the current condition is not confirmed.

access.note: Moved to a private location after sale by the state; no public access found.

events.note: Register's Built field gives 1930; its description says the tower was originally built near Appleton in the late 1930s
SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993 (system-wide closure)

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict left open: the register's Built field says 1930, its description says late 1930s, and no other source read settles it. Current condition is unconfirmed; the only evidence is the 2013 register entry and one Facebook post whose visible text gives no date and may not refer to this tower. That post mentions the poster's grandparents in connection with the tower but is cut off, so no operator is confirmed. The sale and move were in the late 1990s (register) or 199?? (Forest Lookouts), so no event year was assigned. The owner is a private individual named in the register; the story does not name them. Height 80 ft (24.4 m) is the tower height; the register's 207 ft (63 m) is ground elevation and matches the record's elevation_m. The register does not give coordinates for the new site, and it is unclear whether the record's point is the original Appleton site or the moved tower, so the point was not changed.
